title: Major second-line drugs
dek: Fluoroquinolones, bedaquiline, linezolid, pretomanid, and the remaining injectables. BPaLM is the regimen grammar; each drug still has a gene.
story: Once rifampin is lost, the classical HRZE backbone is gone. WHO-preferred all-oral regimens for eligible RR/MDR-TB now center on bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, with or without moxifloxacin (BPaL / BPaLM). Older injectable-based MDR regimens are the historical layer you still read in genomes and in patients who failed them.

Moxifloxacin (and levofloxacin) inhibit DNA gyrase (GyrA/GyrB). QRDR substitutions, especially gyrA A90V, D94G/N/Y, are the usual high-confidence resistance route. Bedaquiline binds the c-ring of ATP synthase (atpE); clinical resistance is more often efflux via MmpL5 overexpression after loss of the negative regulator Rv0678 (mmpR5), which also moves clofazimine MICs.

Linezolid hits the 50S peptidyl-transferase centre (rrl 23S rRNA; rplC L3). Pretomanid (and delamanid) are nitroimidazoles activated by the deazaflavin-dependent nitroreductase Ddn (and F420 biosynthesis genes fbiA/B/C, fgd1). Amikacin/kanamycin still matter as ghosts: rrs 1401 a>g is the canonical 16S map.
deepTitle: Regimen vs gene, and the efflux problem
deep: BPaLM eligibility is a clinical/DST statement (FQ status changes BPaL vs BPaLM). A genome that is FQ-R is not a BPaLM genome. Read the gyrA QRDR before using the acronym.

atpE mutants are rare but high-level for BDQ. Rv0678 frameshifts are common-ish and give modest MIC shifts that can still matter under drug pressure. PepQ and atpE belong on the same plate. Reporting “no atpE mutation, therefore BDQ-S” is incomplete.

Linezolid resistance is still uncommon in many surveys; rrl and rplC are the first places to look. Myelosuppression and neuropathy, not resistance, often limit duration — a pharmacology fact that still changes the genomic prior (less drug exposure, less selection, until it doesn’t).

Cross-resistance: ETH/INH via inhA; BDQ/CFZ via Rv0678; kanamycin/amikacin via rrs; capreomycin additionally cares about tlyA methylation. Draw the Venn diagram before recycling an injectable from an old regimen.

visual.caption: Second-line target map. Efflux (Rv0678 → MmpL5) is drawn as a drug-to-pump relationship because that is how most clinical BDQ resistance actually looks.

example.title: FQ-R and the M in BPaLM
example.setup: An RR-TB isolate has gyrA D94G. atpE, Rv0678, rrl, rplC, ddn, fbiABC are wild type. The ward asks for BPaLM.

steps.title: What D94G means
steps.body: gyrA D94G is a high-confidence FQ-resistance mutation. Moxifloxacin should not be counted as an active companion.

steps.title: Regimen grammar
steps.body: BPaLM is BPaL plus moxifloxacin for FQ-susceptible disease. This genome points at BPaL (or another FQ-sparing WHO-recommended regimen), not at ignoring D94G because “the acronym has an M.”

steps.title: What is still intact
steps.body: No atpE/Rv0678, no rrl/rplC, no Ddn/F420 hits: BDQ, LZD, and Pa do not have a genomic veto from this panel. Phenotype can still surprise; catalogues are priors.

example.takeaway: Read gyrA before you say BPaLM out loud.

check.prompt: Most clinical bedaquiline resistance currently maps to which mechanism?
choices: Loss of Rv0678 leading to MmpL5 efflux, with rare high-level atpE mutants
check.answer: Loss of Rv0678 leading to MmpL5 efflux, with rare high-level atpE mutants
check.why: Efflux regulation is the common clinical route; atpE is the binding-site route and is rarer. rrl is linezolid; katG/pncA are first-line prodrugs.

check.prompt: BPaLM contains bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin. A genome with gyrA A90V is:
choices: FQ-S, so Moxi can be assumed fully active
FQ-R by catalogue, so the M of BPaLM should not be counted as active without a lot of extra evidence
Resistant to pretomanid because A90V is in ddn
check.answer: FQ-R by catalogue, so the M of BPaLM should not be counted as active without a lot of extra evidence
check.why: A90V is a QRDR allele associated with FQ resistance. It is not atpE and not ddn.

whyWrong.FQ-S, so Moxi can be assumed fully activ: A90V is not a susceptible QRDR.
whyWrong.Resistant to pretomanid because A90V is: A90V is gyrA numbering in this question.

check.prompt: On the second-line map, why does BDQ have edges to both AtpE and Rv0678?
check.figureHint: BDQ sits mid-left with two rightward arrows.
choices: Because BDQ is a prodrug activated by both proteins
Because the drug binds ATP synthase, while clinical resistance is often regulatory loss that upregulates efflux
Because Rv0678 is a gyrase subunit
check.answer: Because the drug binds ATP synthase, while clinical resistance is often regulatory loss that upregulates efflux
check.why: Two mechanisms, one drug. The plate is trying to stop the “no atpE mutation ⇒ susceptible” shortcut.

whyWrong.Because BDQ is a prodrug activated by bo: BDQ is direct-acting; Pa/DLM are the nitroimidazole prodrugs.
whyWrong.Because AtpE methylates 16S rRNA: That is a confused rrs/tlyA story.
